transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(Wiping sweat from my brow with a sooty rag, I glance up from poking at the coals with a long iron rod, the forge fire casting dancing shadows on my face.)

"Ah, welcome! Didn't hear you approach over the hammering. Just keeping the coals good and hot, the master's very particular about his fire. What can I do for you today? Looking to commission a new blade, perhaps?"

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
(Affable, despite the warmth of the forge and the many hours already spent at the anvil.)

"Hello! I do hope the heat isn't too much for you. I'm here about a Nichirin sword I recently commissioned. It seems to have... a...let's say, an interesting curve to it that doesn't quite align with its intended function."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I manage a small, slightly strained smile, adjusting the leather apron tied around my waist.)

"Oh, the heat's fine, I'm used to it! Comes with the trade, you know. But... a Nichirin sword, you say? With an interesting curve? Hmm. I wish the master was here to look at it for you, but he's gone on a pilgrimage to the Iron Mountain temple for a special tempering ritual. Won't be back for weeks, I'm afraid, and he's completely out of reach. As for changing a commissioned blade, well... all commissioned Nichirin swords are final sale per guild tradition, you see. Even a Hashira must wait three months for any reforging request to be considered."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
(I take a deep, slow breath, trying to keep my composure, though a sense of urgency seems to be growing within me.)

"Three months? I see. Well, it is what it is. I suppose I'll have to make do until the master returns. I have a feeling this might be a... uniquely challenging time to be short a properly functioning Nichirin."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I nod slowly, my brow furrowed with a touch of genuine sympathy, though my hands remain firmly clasped over the iron rod.)

"Aye, three months, that's the standard, even for... unique situations. I'm just the apprentice, so I can't really override guild rules or try to reach the master where he is. He's very dedicated to his rituals. I do hope it won't cause too much trouble for you in the interim. A Hashira like yourself... I can only imagine the kind of work you face."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
("Hashira" seems to catch in your throat for a moment, but you recover with a small, self-deprecating laugh.)

"Oh, well, the work will keep, won't it? And I can always rely on my... let's call it 'adaptive' techniques. Until the sword is ready, I'll just have to be...a bit more creative in my approach. It's all part of the job, I suppose."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I offer a weak, understanding smile, pulling the iron rod out of the coals and resting it against the forge wall. The heat flares around us for a moment.)

"That's a good way to look at it, I suppose. 'Adaptive techniques.' I'm sure you're more than capable, given your rank. Still, it's a shame about the wait. Is there anything else I can help you with today, then? Perhaps some general maintenance supplies? Sharpening stones, polishing cloths, blade oil? We've got a good stock of those, at least."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
(You consider the offer for a moment, nodding with a bit of relief as you realize that some smaller items could be quite useful.)

"Actually, that's a great idea. I could use a couple of sharpening stones and a few cloths, if that's not too much trouble. And some oil, of course. While I'm waiting for the new blade, it's not a bad idea to keep my current ones in prime condition. Maintenance is key, after all."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(My face brightens considerably at the prospect of an actual, doable task.)

"Oh, absolutely! No trouble at all, I can definitely help with that! Good quality stones, plenty of cloths, and the finest blade oil we've got. Maintenance *is* key, you're right. Especially when you've got to make a blade last a bit longer than planned. Just a moment, let me fetch those for you from the back."

(I turn and head towards a dusty corner of the smithy, lined with shelves holding various tools and supplies.)

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
(You watch me go, a bit of your earlier urgency replaced by a sense of... not quite contentment, but acceptance. At least, for now, you have something to focus on that can help you be ready when the Nichirin finally arrives.)

"Thank you, that's very kind of you. While you're fetching those, I can check out the selection of...let's say 'customary' snacks you mentioned earlier. A bit of sustenance could be welcome after all this travel and waiting. Care to join me?"

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I pause, halfway to the shelves, and turn back, a small, slightly embarrassed smile on my face.)

"Oh, uh, thank you for the offer, but I really should stay with the forge. The master expects me to keep the coals at a precise temperature, especially when he's away. Can't let the fire die down, or it'll take ages to get it back up to snuff. But please, feel free to help yourself to anything on the small table by the corner – dried persimmons, rice crackers... whatever catches your eye!"

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
("Ah, the demands of an exacting master and an exacting craft," you say with a wry understanding, not quite hiding your own relief at the freedom to explore the treat selection.)

"Of course, I understand completely. No need to apologize! I'll just...be over here, then, in case you need any assistance with the items you're getting. Or if you want to chat about the forge, or...well, anything, really. I'm not averse to a bit of company while waiting for the universe to catch up with my schedule."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I turn back to the shelves, rummaging through a box for the sharpening stones, a faint *clink* sound echoing in the smithy.)

"No need to apologize at all, Hashira Kanroji! Just doing my duty. And I appreciate the company, it can get a bit quiet in here sometimes with just the fire for conversation. Found some good fine-grit stones here, perfect for a keen edge. And a stack of new cloths. Just need to grab the oil now."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
("The company is most appreciated, and it's a reminder that we're all part of a larger...let's call it 'web of industry' for want of a better term," you say, now seated at the table, a small pile of snacks before you.)

"Take your time, and when you're done, we can compare notes on what makes a good edge. I've always been fascinated by the craftsmanship that goes into creating a tool that can slice through... well, you know the rest. There's a certain art to it, isn't there?"

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I emerge from the back with a small bottle of dark, viscous oil and set it down on a nearby workbench next to the stones and cloths, carefully. I then turn to face her, wiping my hands on my apron.)

"A 'web of industry,' I like that! And yes, there's definitely an art to it, Hashira Kanroji. A really good edge, it's not just about sharpness, is it? It's about how long it *holds* that sharpness, how it feels through the cut. The master always says the blade needs to feel like an extension of the wielder, not just a tool. That's why the tempering is so crucial, to give it that perfect balance of strength and flexibility."

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
(You reach out to take the oil from the workbench, your touch gentle but deliberate, and carefully examine the label, then the liquid itself.)
"An extension of the wielder, that's a beautiful way to put it. And you're right, it's not just about the initial cut, but the *long* cut, as it were. The balance you're talking about is...well, it's what separates a tool from a true companion. I have a feeling that the wait for this new blade will be worth it, just from our conversation here. It's given me a bit more patience."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I watch her examine the oil, a sense of pride swelling in my chest, even though it's the master's work and reputation she's praising.)

"It absolutely will be worth it, Hashira Kanroji. The master puts his heart and soul into every blade, truly. He says a Nichirin sword isn't just metal; it's forged spirit. He'd be very pleased to hear you say that about patience. It takes a lot of it to make a truly great sword, and I suppose, to wield one too."

(I gesture towards the sharpening stones and cloths.)

"So, these should serve you well until the master returns. Anything else I can fetch for you before you head off?"

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
(You place the oil into a cloth bag along with the stones and cloths, securing it with a practiced knot.)

"Thank you, you've been more than helpful. I'll take my leave now, but I'll be back to check on the new blade's progress when I can. In the meantime, I'll have to rely on your...let's say 'extended metaphor' about the spirit of the sword to keep me company. Take care, and tell the master I'm looking forward to trying out his creation when it's ready."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I bow my head slightly, a polite gesture, as she gathers her supplies.)

"Of course, Hashira Kanroji! I'll be sure to relay your message to the master the moment he returns. He'll be glad to hear it. And I'll make sure the forge stays hot and ready for when he starts on your reforging. Until then, please take care on your travels, and stay safe out there!"

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
(With a final, warm smile, you pick up the bag and prepare to leave, pausing at the threshold to look back.)

"Thank you for your hospitality, and for your work. Both are greatly appreciated. May the coals in your forge always glow with the same warmth you've shown me today. Take care, and...well, I'll see you on the other side of this reforging, I suppose."
